newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal stable, more supply seen this month.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal stable, more supply seen this month.

text.p: Thai soymeal prices were mostly stable this week as more supplies were coming to market later in the month, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Corn prices were also steady in a moderate trade, they said.

Despite forecast of bullish demand for soymeal next year, no buyers have placed orders to cover next year's demand as soybean prices remained high and the demand for 1996 has been fully covered, trade sources said.
Soymeal prices were quoted at around 9.60 baht ($0.38) and corn at 4.30-4.40 baht a kg, barely changed from last week, they said.
"There's no activity in the market. The industry sees no rush to buy at the moment," one trader said. "The local soymeal prices could ease next week as more supplies are seen coming to the market."
About 20,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal is expected to arrive in Thailand on Saturday and 45,000 tonnes more will arrive on Monday, according to shipping sources.
Thai animal feed industry forecast that the demand for soymeal in 1997 could reach 1.7 million tonnes from 1.3-1.4 million tonnes expected this year.
Of the total, more than one million tonnes are expected to be directly imported, they said.
The industry predicted that about 670,000 tonnes of soymeal will be produced domestically from soybean, both local and imported, by oil crushers for oil extraction.
